retrieval.text: Adam was the chosen of the Most High, formed of the dust of the ground and given the breath of life, which is the commandments (Genesis 2:7). The serpent is Satan, who taught Eve doctrine, that she would not die, and played on her envy, the desire to be equal (Genesis 3:1-5; Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). The fruit she ate was the lie, and she taught her husband what the serpent had taught her (Genesis 3:6). Their nakedness was sin, and the sin was idolatry (Genesis 3:7; Exodus 32:25). The Lord covered them with the first sacrifice and drove them out of the garden (Genesis 3:21-24).

retrieval.title: Abel
retrieval.text: Abel was a keeper of sheep and Cain a tiller of the ground, and with them comes the birth of trade and of religion (Genesis 4:1-2). Abel brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof, in accordance with the sacrifice ordained when the Lord made coats of skins, and the Lord had respect unto him (Genesis 4:4; Genesis 3:21). Abel was a prophet, and when Cain talked with him he was trying to get Cain to repent; Cain slew him (Genesis 4:8; Matthew 23:35). His righteousness still speaks, though he is dead (Hebrews 11:4).

retrieval.text: Lamech of Cain’s line took two wives, the first time scripture records a man taking multiple wives, and it was the sons of the wicked who did it (Genesis 4:19). His sons held the trades of that line: cattle and produce, music, and weapons (Genesis 4:20-22).
